process_area.title: Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics

fields.Participants: PMO, FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-33.2), Sponsor, Business Owner, BI (links to VS-28.1), Strategy (links to VS-33)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-measure of "measurement method, owner, and realization timeline" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validate benefits realization post-go-live" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report benefits realization at portfolio level to executives" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: disciplined baselines and validation; operational: control-group/methodology
Pain Points / Risks: - **Benefit-overstatement risk**: Projected benefits not realized; mitigated by disciplined baselines and validation
- **Attribution-ambiguity risk**: Hard to isolate project benefit from macro; mitigated by control-group/methodology
System Touchpoints: - FP&A/performance (links to VS-17.4/VS-33.2); BI (links to VS-28.1); domain analytics (links to VS-109/W3491/VS-108/W3468/VS-40/W2748); PMIS (links to W3562)

steps.activity: PMO/Sponsor define the benefits plan per project: benefit types (financial — revenue/cost/cash; non-financial — customer/NPS links to VS-13, operational, regulatory, ESG links to VS-25), baselines, targets, measurement method, owner, and realization timeline; align to the business case (W3551)

PMO/FP&A track and validate benefits realization post-go-live: measure actual vs target (links to domain analytics, e.g., store sales lift links to VS-109/W3491, capex ROI links to VS-40/W2748, ESG links to VS-108/W3468), validate attribution, and identify shortfalls/root-cause

PMO/Strategy report benefits realization at portfolio level to executives (links to VS-33.2) and governance (W3552), manage shortfalls (corrective action, re-baseline), and feed outcomes to portfolio prioritization (W3547) and lessons (W3560)

fields.Participants: PMO, IT (links to VS-27/VS-99), BI (links to VS-28), Master Data (links to VS-29), Finance (links to VS-40), Vendors

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documents, dashboards/reporting, and integration to ERP/BI" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "report PMIS health/adoption to PMO governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: training, integration, and mandate; operational: integration
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-adoption risk**: Tool unused, data stale; mitigated by training, integration, and mandate
- **Integration-gap risk**: PMIS disconnected from ERP/capex causes double-entry; mitigated by integration
System Touchpoints: - IT ops/security (links to VS-27/VS-27.3); IT asset (links to VS-99); capex integration (links to VS-40); HR (links to VS-19); finance (links to VS-17); BI/data quality (links to VS-28/VS-28.2)

steps.activity: PMO/IT define the PMIS requirements: portfolio/project/program register, WBS/scheduling, resource/capacity, budget/cost (integrate to capex links to VS-40), risk/issue/change, documents, dashboards/reporting, and integration to ERP/BI (links to VS-28/VS-17); select/configure the tool

IT/PMO implement and integrate the PMIS: configure, integrate to ERP/capex (links to VS-40/W1811), HR (links to VS-19), finance (links to VS-17), and BI (links to VS-28); manage access/roles, security (links to VS-27.3), and data quality (links to VS-28.2)

PMO/IT maintain the PMIS: support/training (links to VS-19.4), user adoption, enhancements, and the tool lifecycle (links to VS-99); report PMIS health/adoption to PMO governance (W3552) and maturity (W3565)

fields.Participants: PMO, BI (links to VS-28.1), Strategy (links to VS-33.2), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Executive Committee

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "PMO/BI compute portfolio KPIs" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "methodology gaps, and at-risk projects/programs" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: data governance (links to VS-28); operational: balanced KPIs and audit
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-quality risk**: Poor PMIS data undermines analytics; mitigated by data governance (links to VS-28.2)
- **KPI-gaming risk**: KPIs manipulated to look good; mitigated by balanced KPIs and audit
System Touchpoints: - BI/analytics (links to VS-28.1); PMIS (links to W3562); strategy/performance (links to VS-33.2); finance (links to VS-17.4); dashboards (links to W3552)

steps.activity: PMO/BI compute portfolio KPIs: on-time/on-budget %, schedule/cost performance index (SPI/CPI), stage-gate compliance (W3548), benefits realization (W3561), resource utilization (W3553), risk/issue counts (W3558), and portfolio throughput/cycle-time; benchmark vs targets and industry

PMO/Strategy analyze portfolio trends and root causes: chronic slippage/overrun categories, resource bottlenecks, methodology gaps, and at-risk projects/programs; recommend portfolio/corrective actions

PMO publish the portfolio performance analytics to executives (links to VS-33.2) and governance (W3552), drive data-informed decisions, and feed insights to maturity/CI (W3565) and methodology (W3548)

fields.Participants: Finance (links to VS-40/VS-17.4), PMO, FP&A, Sponsor, Audit (links to VS-21), Treasury (links to VS-18)

workflows.name: Program / Project Financial Performance vs Business Case

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-reconcile of "reconcile project/program financial performance vs the approved business case" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-schedule of "identify financial performance drivers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report program/project financial performance to executives" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: benchmarking and lessons; operational: finance review (links to VS-40/W1823)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Estimate-inaccuracy risk**: Recurring over-optimism in business cases; mitigated by benchmarking and lessons
- **Capitalization-error risk**: Wrong capex/OpEx split distorts financials; mitigated by finance review (links to VS-40/W1823)
System Touchpoints: - Capex (links to VS-40/W1825/W1828/W1823/W2750); treasury/cash (links to VS-18); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); audit (links to VS-21); PMIS (links to W3562)

steps.activity: Finance/PMO reconcile project/program financial performance vs the approved business case (W3551): actual cost vs budget (links to VS-40/W1825), actual capex vs CIP/asset turnover (links to VS-40/W1828), cash/timing (links to VS-18), and financial benefits realized (W3561); compute payback/IRR vs plan

Finance/PMO identify financial performance drivers (estimate accuracy, change-orders W3556, scope/schedule, market), manage write-offs for abandoned/under-performing projects (links to VS-40/W2750), and ensure proper capitalization (links to VS-40/W1823)

Finance/PMO report program/project financial performance to executives (links to VS-33.2), audit (links to VS-21), and governance (W3552); feed financial lessons to estimation (W3551) and maturity (W3565)

fields.Participants: PMO Director, PMO, Audit (links to VS-21), Strategy (links to VS-33), HR/L&D (links to VS-19.4), Executive Committee

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "methodology adoption, tooling, resource capability, governance, and benefits" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "report maturity progress and CI outcomes to executives" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: maturity assessment and CI roadmap; operational: training/certification (links to VS-19)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Maturity-stagnation risk**: PMO capability plateaus; mitigated by maturity assessment and CI roadmap
- **Capability-gap risk**: PM skills lag project complexity; mitigated by training/certification (links to VS-19.4)
System Touchpoints: - Audit (links to VS-21); strategy (links to VS-33); L&D (links to VS-19.4); PMIS (links to W3562); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: PMO Director/Audit assess PMO maturity against a model (e.g., OPM3/P3M3): portfolio/program/project management capability, methodology adoption, tooling, resource capability, governance, and benefits realization; identify gaps vs target maturity

PMO Director develop and execute the maturity/CI roadmap: methodology enhancements (W3548/W3566), tooling (W3562), capability/training (links to VS-19.4 — PMP/PRINCE2/Agile certification), governance tuning, and process improvement; manage via the PMO itself
PMO Director report maturity progress and CI outcomes to executives (links to VS-33.2) and governance (W3552), and feed to the PMO charter/strategy (W3545); benchmark vs industry maturity

fields.Participants: PMO, Delivery Leads (links to VS-20/VS-37/VS-109/VS-108/VS-27), Quality (links to VS-31), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Knowledge Mgmt (links to VS-30.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "PMO maintain the project-management standards and methodology portfolio" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-schedule of "schedule, risk/issue/change registers, status reports, closure/lessons, RACI,…" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: centralized standards; operational: tiered/tailored methodology
Pain Points / Risks: - **Template-proliferation risk**: Inconsistent/outdated templates; mitigated by centralized standards
- **Methodology-rigidity risk**: One-size-fits-all methodology stifles domain-appropriate approaches; mitigated by tiered/tailored methodology
System Touchpoints: - Knowledge base (links to VS-30.3/VS-88); L&D (links to VS-19.4); domain methodology (links to VS-20/VS-27/W132/VS-31); PMIS/templates (links to W3562)

steps.activity: PMO maintain the project-management standards and methodology portfolio: lifecycle/stage-gate (W3548), delivery approaches (waterfall/Agile/hybrid per project type), PMBOK/PRINCE2/Agile/Scrum standards, and integration with domain methodologies (construction links to VS-20, IT/SDLC links to VS-27/W132, quality links to VS-31)

PMO maintain the templates and knowledge assets: charter, business case, WBS/schedule, risk/issue/change registers, status reports, closure/lessons, RACI, and domain templates; publish to the knowledge base (links to VS-30.3/VS-88)
PMO evolve standards/templates from lessons (W3560), maturity (W3565), and industry best-practice; train project managers/community-of-practice (links to VS-19.4); ensure adoption and consistency

fields.Participants: PMO, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34/VS-67), Project Managers, Legal (links to VS-100.3), Finance (links to VS-40), Vendor/Contractor
fields.Trigger: Vendor/contractor on project (links to VS-03/VS-34); QBR cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "Project Manager/PMO manage vendor/contractor performance on the project" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "PMO/Procurement conduct vendor/contractor QBR and scorecard" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: contract terms (LD, warranty) and scorecard; operational: framework competition
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-underperformance risk**: Contractor misses scope/schedule/quality; mitigated by contract terms (LD, warranty) and scorecard
- **Vendor-concentration risk**: Over-reliance on one contractor; mitigated by framework competition
System Touchpoints: - Vendor/contract (links to VS-03/VS-34/VS-100.3); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67/W3512); HSE (links to VS-24); capex (links to VS-40/W1820); PMIS (links to W3562)

steps.activity: PMO/Procurement govern project vendors/contractors: framework/master agreements across the program (links to VS-03/VS-34), pre-qualification/accreditation, scope/contract allocation, and integration to vendor management (links to VS-03.3/VS-67); manage EPC/GC/consultant relationships (e.g., links to VS-108/W3452, VS-109/W3482)

Project Manager/PMO manage vendor/contractor performance on the project: scope/schedule/quality/cost delivery (W3554–W3557), HSE (links to VS-24), contract compliance (milestones, LD, warranty links to VS-100.3), and issue/claim management; manage SLA and change (W3556)

PMO/Procurement conduct vendor/contractor QBR and scorecard (links to VS-67/W3512 methodology): performance, quality, HSE, commercial, and relationship; manage consequences (growth/probation/exit), feed the vendor master/scorecard (links to VS-03/VS-67), and report to governance (W3552)

fields.Participants: PMO, Transformation/Innovation (links to VS-30), Change Mgmt, HR/EX (links to VS-103.2), Strategy (links to VS-33), Communications (links to VS-14.3), Executive Committee

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enterprise transformation portfolio" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate change across concurrent projects/programs to avoid change-fatigue" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track transformation outcomes and adoption" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-567 (ensure controlled execution — Project Benefits Realization, PMIS & PMO Analytics (PA-112.3).)
- operational: portfolio sequencing and change-load management; operational: change-management and adoption tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Change-fatigue risk**: Concurrent transformations overwhelm the organization; mitigated by portfolio sequencing and change-load management
- **Adoption-failure risk**: Solutions delivered but not adopted; mitigated by change-management and adoption tracking
System Touchpoints: - Transformation/digital (links to VS-30); strategy (links to VS-33); HR/EX/change (links to VS-103.2); comms (links to VS-14.3); L&D (links to VS-19.4); board reporting (links to VS-36); benefits (links to W3561)

steps.activity: PMO/Transformation govern the enterprise transformation portfolio: strategic transformations (e.g., digital/ERP links to VS-27/VS-30, omnichannel links to VS-60, net-zero links to VS-25/VS-108, operating-model change), structure as programs (W3549), and align to corporate strategy (links to VS-33); integrate change-management (links to VS-103.2)

Change Mgmt/PMO manage organizational change across the portfolio: stakeholder engagement (W3559), communication (links to VS-14.3/VS-103.2), training/adoption (links to VS-19.4), resistance management, and business readiness; coordinate change across concurrent projects/programs to avoid change-fatigue

PMO/Transformation track transformation outcomes and adoption (links to VS-103/W3561), report to executives (links to VS-33.2) and Board (links to VS-36), and feed learnings to maturity (W3565) and strategy (links to VS-33); manage the transformation portfolio within the overall project portfolio (W3545)
